phases.title: LookML extractor
phases.goal: Parse .view.lkml / .model.lkml / .dashboard.lookml so graphify understands Looker views, explores/joins, and dashboard tiles.
phases.status: complete, pushed, PR not yet opened (human step)
key_design_decisions: Two incompatible LookML dashboard grammars exist in the wild: brace-syntax 'dashboards-next' (parsed by the lkml package) and legacy list-of-dicts YAML starting with '---' (parsed by PyYAML). Extractor tries lkml first, falls back to PyYAML, then gives up gracefully.
Worked around a real lkml package parser gap: 'sorts: [field asc|desc]' direction suffixes inside a plain list raise a SyntaxError. Stripped via regex (_strip_sort_directions) before parsing.

derived_table SQL bodies get a best-effort FROM/JOIN regex scan (INFERRED confidence) that explicitly excludes CTE names defined via WITH/AS in the same body, so a CTE alias is never mistaken for a physical table.

All nodes keyed by bare name via make_id — this is the convention Phase 2 also adopted, so a LookML view's sql_table_name and a same-named dbt model resolve to ONE node when graphs are combined with `graphify merge-graphs`.

phases.title: dbt manifest.json lineage extractor
phases.goal: Read dbt's already-resolved ref()/source() lineage from target/manifest.json, since dbt models are Jinja templates that graphify's tree-sitter-sql extractor cannot parse (verified empirically: extract_sql on real dbt .sql model files produces 1 node / 0 edges — Jinja isn't valid SQL, and dbt only adds the CREATE TABLE/VIEW wrapper at run time).
phases.status: complete, pushed, PR not yet opened (human step)
key_design_decisions: Recognized by CONTENT, not filename alone: manifest.json is also the standard PWA/web-app-manifest filename. Detection reads only the first 4KB and sniffs for the dbt_schema_version marker key — never loads the whole (potentially 10MB+) file just to check.

Lives as a top-level graphify/*.py sibling to manifest_ingest.py / mcp_ingest.py, NOT under graphify/extractors/ — that directory is for suffix-dispatched per-language extractors only; this one is content-sniffed and checked earlier in _get_extractor.

Nodes keyed by bare name via make_id(name), matching Phase 1's lookml.py convention exactly — this is what lets `graphify merge-graphs` collapse a dbt model and a LookML view's backing table into one node across repos with no special-cased cross-extractor edge type.

test and analysis resource types excluded deliberately — assertions/ad-hoc queries, not physical data lineage. Verified against a real 1600+-node manifest: excluding them roughly halves the extracted node count vs. the raw manifest.

phases.title: dbt SQL-body parsing (compiled model bodies, not just inter-model lineage)
phases.goal: Phase 2 only gives model-to-model/source depends_on edges from manifest.json's metadata — it does not parse the actual SQL body of a dbt model (which fields it selects, which CTEs it defines, etc.), because graphify's tree-sitter-sql extractor can't parse the raw Jinja-templated .sql source.
proposed_approach: Run `dbt compile` (not `dbt parse`) so target/manifest.json's compiled_code field is populated with fully Jinja-resolved SQL for every model.

For each model, wrap compiled_code in a synthetic 'CREATE VIEW <model_name> AS <compiled_sql>' shadow file, since graphify's existing extract_sql only activates on top-level CREATE TABLE/VIEW/etc. statements, never bare SELECT.

Feed the shadow files to graphify's existing extract_sql — no new graphify code needed for this phase, just a pre-processing script in the dbt repo (or a wrapper invoked before `graphify path/to/shadow_dir`).
phases.blocking_open_item: A prior attempt to test the CREATE VIEW-wrapping approach was blocked by this environment's own tool-safety filter (flagged for containing literal 'CREATE VIEW' text in a test command) — never actually verified end-to-end. First task of this phase must be confirming the wrap-and-parse approach actually produces useful nodes/edges on a real compiled model before building any tooling around it.
